content: Open 1 of a major (1♥ or 1♠) with 12–21 HCP and a 5+ card major. With two 5-card majors, open the higher one (spades).
Open 1NT with exactly 15–17 HCP and a balanced hand (4-3-3-3, 4-4-3-2, or 5-3-3-2) and no 5-card major.
Open 1 of a minor with 12–21 HCP and no 5-card major. Open your longer minor; with 4-4, open 1♦; with 3-3, open 1♣.
With fewer than 12 HCP, pass. You need opening strength before you describe your hand with a bid.
Myth: “My hand is strong, so I should open 1NT.” 1NT is about shape and a narrow 15–17 range, not just strength. With a 5-card major, open the major instead.
Myth: “I have 11 HCP so I should open.” 11 is below the 12-point opening bar. Recount, and if you are truly under 12, pass.
♠KQ874 ♥A3 ♦K92 ♣J54 is 13 HCP with 5 spades. Open 1♠, not 1NT — you hold a 5-card major.
Look at your longest suit. How many cards do you have in it?
Count your high-card points. Is your hand in the opening range?
